newsitem.title: LIECHTENSTEIN: SOCCER-MACEDONIA HIT 11 BUT JUST MISS RECORD WORLD CUP WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MACEDONIA HIT 11 BUT JUST MISS RECORD WORLD CUP WIN.

text.p: Macedonia scored one of the biggest wins in World Cup history when they crushed the part-timers of Liechtenstein 11-1 in a group eight qualifer on Saturday.

The result was the joint-fourth highest victory in the tournament's 66-year history folowing New Zealand's 13-0 win over Fiji in 1982, West Germany's 12-0 win over Cyprus in 1970 and Mexico's 11-0 win over St Vincent in 1993.
The only other previous matches to end 11-1 were when Trinidad beat Antigua in 1974 and Hungary beat Greece in 1938.
With slightly more luck Macedonia could have even achieved an all-time record, but one defensive error allowed Liechtenstein a consolation and the visitors also missed a couple of sitters.

Dejvi Gavevski led the rout with a hat-trick after opening the scoring in the eighth minute and making it 2-0 after 13 minutes with a diving header. He scored his third after 60 minutes which put his team 9-0 up.
Mitko Stojkovski, Toni Micevski and Sasa Ciric all scored two while Georgi Hristov and Vanco Micevski added the others.
Franz Schaedler gave the home fans something to cheer with a lone goal after 79 minutes.

Macedonia's huge victory moved them up from fourth to first in the standings on seven points ahead of Ireland, Romania and Lithuania who are all on six points. Ireland have a chance to move back on top if they beat Iceland on Sunday.

Macedonia went in 6-0 up at half-time with a record score clearly within their sights and they maintained their spree early in the second half when Micevski chipped a shot over beleaguered Liechtenstein keeper Martin Heeb in the 49th minute to put Macedonia 7-0 up.
Schaedler prevented a total whitewash when he chested the ball past a startled Macedonian keeper Danco Celeski in the 79th minute scoring what was only Liechtenstein's second ever World Cup goal.

Lineups: Liechtenstein: 1-Martin Heeb, 2-Juergen Ospelt, 3-Daniel Telser (Martin Telser 53rd), 4-Roland Hilti (Herbert Bicker 48th), 5- Thomas Hanselmann, 6-Ralf Oehri, 7-Alexander Quaderer (Patrik Marxer 73rd), 8-Harry Zech, 9-Franz Schaedler, 10-Daniel Hasler, 11-Stefan Hassler Macedonia: 1-Danco Celeski, 2-Goce Sedloski, 3-Mitko Stojkovski (Saso Milosevski 65th), 4-Ljupco Markovski, 5-Igor-Sasa Nikolovski, 6-Srdjan Zaharievski, 7-Valatko Gosev, 8-Toni Micevski (Toni Naumsoki 73rd), 9-Georgi Hristov, 10-Sasa Ciric, 11-Dejvi Gavevski (Vanco Micevski 70th)
